In the nonvertical chart the section is X=Hb/(H+1−a·b), a·b≤1. Multiplication of the area pullback by a·X changes the denominator exponent from d to d+1 and supplies a positive scalar, so the actual vertical mean has the opposite sign of the displayed integral.

The pushforward density along a·b is bounded and even. For d>2, an intermediate slice between −q and q contains the appropriate Minkowski combination of the two equal-volume slices, giving monotonicity by ordinary Brunn–Minkowski. In d=2 it is constant on a symmetric interval. In every case it is positive near zero.

Pair q and −q for 0<R≤1, obtaining a strictly positive integral. For finite R≥1 the omitted tail below −R is strictly negative. The full tail integral equals (H+1)/(d H^d)−1/[(d−1)H^(d−1)]=(d−1−H)/[d(d−1)H^d]. Its zero at H=d−1 still leaves strict positivity for every finite interval.

Layer cake decomposes the even monotone projection density into symmetric intervals. The support is bounded and the denominator on the truncated domain is bounded below by H, so signed Fubini is valid. The positive-density region yields positive-length intervals for a positive set of levels.

The horizontal section is the centered scale H/(H+1) of D. For a vertical section, symmetry gives zero horizontal first moment and E[r]=(d−1)/d under the cross-section factor r^(d−2). Thus mean height H−(H+1)E[r]=(H−(d−1))/d, including the d=2 interval.

dependencies.mapping: Use m=d−1, apex height H, arbitrary centrally symmetric D, and nonvertical raw normal (a,1). Its formula is for actual d-volume and Euclidean section area divided by the norm of that raw normal. The factor is positive and independent of the section point, so the first moment sign transfers exactly.

overlap.comparison: Gives the exact oblique section chart and centroid criterion for all H>0. It does not resolve the strict sign of the vertical section moment for the full symmetric-base class or the vertical-plane case.

Bounds a corrected cap record for centered laws of scalar slopes on a particular weighted cone. It does not classify all actual sections of arbitrary uniform symmetric-base pyramids or state the height sign.

readability: The word oblique excludes both horizontal and vertical planes. The phrase 'central symmetric section' means a section through the center of a centrally symmetric base.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: For every centrally symmetric convex base and 0<H≤d−1, each oblique through-zero section has strictly negative mean height. The horizontal and vertical centroid formulas give the stated complete classification.
